newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan policeman resigns after failed police search.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan policeman resigns after failed police search.

text.p: Taiwan's top police superintendent on Thursday offered his resignation over police failure to arrest the island's three most wanted men.
"I have offered my resignation to the interior minister to...take responsiblity over police (failure) in apprehending the three suspects," Yao told reporters.

The three, who are being sought over the abduction and murder of the teenage daughter of a popular actress in April, further embarrassed police on Wednesday by making off with T$4 million (US$143,000) in ransom money from a businessmen.
The businessman was kidnapped and freed last week after paying the ransom, and the case was made public on Wednesday.
Angry legislators of ruling and opposition parties on Thursday said police were powerless and demanded that Yao step down to take responsibility.
The kidnap and murder of 17-year-old Pai Hsiao-yen, daughter of popular actress Pai Ping-ping, shocked the island.

The crime rekindled anger over the failure of police to solve the gangland-style murder of Taoyuan county magistrate and seven others in his home last November or the murder of an opposition leader in southern Taiwan two weeks later.
More than 50,000 people marched in Taipei on May 4 to denounce Pai's gruesome murder and rising crime. They demanded Premier Lien Chan's resignation and a cabinet reshuffle.
